chunks: From him, from Ja'far, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yn, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'They do not increase in honor through Islam except us; we inherit them and they do not inherit us. This is the inheritance of Abu Talib in our hands, so we do not consider it except in the child and the parent, and we do not consider it in the husband and the wife.'

key_terms.مِيرَاثُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Inheritance of Abu Talib (referring to the specific ruling for the Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from the Ahl al-Bayt and who do they inherit from according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *al-mirath li-man shaya al-millata* (inheritance to the one who shares the faith), asserting that the Ahl al-Bayt inherit from non-Shia relatives while the reverse is not true. This ruling, rooted in the precedent of Abu Talib, is specifically limited to direct vertical lineage (parents and children) and excludes horizontal spousal inheritance, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view that marital bonds do not override religious affiliation in inheritance matters.
